macros.name: abstractname
macros.doc: You may use \abstractname{⟨text⟩} to change the abstract caption to text.

macros.name: advisor
macros.doc: Give the name of your advisor with the \advisor macro.

macros.name: dedicationname
macros.doc: You may use \dedicationname{⟨text⟩} to change the title for the dedication page.

macros.name: degaward
macros.doc: Specify the degree you’re aiming for with the \degaward macro.

macros.name: makecopyright
macros.doc: The \makecopyright macro should be invoked after \maketitle to produce a copyright page.

macros.name: maketitle
macros.doc: The title page is generated by \maketitle with no arguments.

macros.name: normalspacing
macros.doc: Text is formatted in \normalspacing i.e. doublespacing.

macros.name: prefacename
macros.doc: You may use \prefacename to change the name of this section.

macros.name: secondadvisor
macros.doc: Give the name of your second advisor, if any, with the \secondadvisor macro.

macros.name: sym
macros.doc: The command \sym{⟨symbol⟩}{⟨definition⟩} may make the task of entering the symbols and their meanings in the symbols environment easier. \sym takes two arguments: the first, a math “object” and the second, the plain text describing the symbol.

macros.name: symbolsname
macros.doc: You may use \symbolsname{} to change the title of the symbols section.

macros.name: title
macros.doc: The title of the document, using the \title macro.

macros.name: unnumchapter
macros.doc: Allows the user to create unnumbered chapters that appear in the TOC.

envs.name: abstract
envs.doc: The abstract text should be placed between \begin{abstract} and \end{abstract}.

envs.name: dedication
envs.doc: The format of dedication is essentially free. This environment will center the text of your dedication vertically on the page.

envs.name: preface
envs.doc: The preface environment is provided for formatting the preface to your work.

envs.name: symbols
envs.doc: Use the symbols envrionment to format a list of symbols/abbreviations used in your work.

envs.name: symbols
envs.doc: Use the symbols envrionment to format a list of symbols/abbreviations used in your work.
